_comment: Freeze-proof system-protection policy — single source of truth, consumed by BOTH configuration_system-protection.nix (builtins.fromJSON, boot-time enforcement) AND build.sh (_apply_daemon_caps, live enforcement before every nix build). Hardware: Surface Pro 8, 8 logical CPUs, 8GB RAM, NVMe (none scheduler), zram swap + disk hibernate swapfile. The machine froze 10x because nix builds (running inside nix-daemon, NOT the client) ballooned RAM and thrashed pages to the disk swapfile. The fix layers: (1) nix-daemon hard-capped with MemorySwapMax=0 so a runaway build OOM-kills a compile job instead of swap-thrashing; (2) the GUI session gets guaranteed unreclaimable RAM; (3) an UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (reserved RAM + realtime CPU + realtime IO) hosts the killers (freeze-guard, plus the now-disabled earlyoom) and the mesh (sshd/rescue) so they can ALWAYS act even when everything else is starved; (4) 2026-07-03 user directive 'ONLY PSI, remove ALL non-PSI triggers' — systemd-oomd (memory PSI) + freeze-guard (mem/io/cpu PSI active killer) are the ONLY two active killers; earlyoom (absolute mem%/swap%, zero PSI awareness) is disabled (sysprot.earlyoom.enable=false), kept data-driven so it can be re-enabled later if ever wanted.

nix_daemon._comment: Hard caps on nix-daemon.service — the ACTUAL build worker (cc1plus/rustc/ld run as its cgroup children). MemorySwapMax=0 = the build subtree can NEVER swap (not zram, not the disk swapfile) → the kernel OOM-kills one compile job instead of thrashing the disk → the desktop never freezes. cgroup v2 memory.max on the parent caps the whole subtree. Applied LIVE before every build by build.sh because 'nixos-rebuild switch' reloads unit files but does NOT re-apply resource control to the already-running daemon (this drift left the live daemon at 6G/4G-swap and caused the freezes).

gui_session._comment: user-1000.slice (the KDE Plasma desktop). MemoryMin = RAM the kernel is FORBIDDEN to reclaim, so the compositor (kwin/plasmashell) stays responsive under build pressure. 2026-07-02 FIX: MemorySwapMax=0 also blocked ZRAM (cgroup swap caps can't distinguish zram from disk) — with MemoryHigh below the real working set the kernel could only evict file-backed pages (running executables), which faulted straight back through kcryptd/btrfs = the freeze. 2026-07-03: valve 2G→6G — the 2G valve saturated (Redroid + multi-claude workload), reclaim had nowhere to spill while 17G of zram sat FREE, MemAvailable collapsed to 2% and earlyoom killed sessions/imports at near-zero PSI. 6G still lands zram-first (prio 100 vs disk -1); the disk swapfile is touched only after ~7.6G compressed zram truly fills.

reservation._comment: THE UNTOUCHABLE ISLAND (user requirement: 'watchdog+mesh MUST HAVE ownership of a never-touched area of disk+memory+cpu to ALWAYS kill whatever overwhelms the system'). Hosts: freeze-guard, earlyoom, sshd, rescue-ssh (connectivity.slice). MemoryMin = guaranteed unreclaimable RAM. CPU = SCHED_FIFO realtime priority preempts ALL normal processes even at 100% load. IO = realtime ioprio class always gets the NVMe queue. OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 = NEVER killed. So the killers + remote rescue can always run, no matter what.

watchdog._comment: freeze-guard: an ACTIVE PSI killer running in the untouchable island. PSI IS THE ONLY KILL METRIC (no absolute CPU%/RSS/mem% triggers — those cause false kills at PSI=0). Every interval_sec it reads /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}: mem/io use 'full avg10' (% of last 10s ALL tasks stalled); cpu uses 'some avg10' (a pure spin stalls some tasks, rarely all). ONLY when a signal exceeds its limit does it act — killing the top offender and re-checking, walking down the rank up to max_kills_per_tick times until pressure drops. Victim RANKING (not trigger) is pressure-aware: CPU breach ranks by %cpu, mem/io breach by RSS; prefer_kill (compilers/browsers) first, then any non-avoid_kill process. Kills are GRACEFUL SIGTERM for node/claude (so Claude Code prints its resume hint), SIGKILL for everything else. Backstop beneath cgroup caps + systemd-oomd. Baked into the service script at build time (reproducible); every action echoed to the journal.

watchdog_selfcheck._comment: 2026-07-04 freeze incident root cause: freeze-guard.service was manually stopped (sudo systemctl stop) during debugging at 09:03 and never restarted; the desktop froze 3h22m later with cpuPSI(some)=85%/memPSI(full)=44% (both above freeze-guard's own trigger thresholds) with NO killer running. 'nixos-rebuild switch' does NOT re-arm a manually-stopped-but-unchanged enabled unit — switch-to-configuration only starts/restarts units whose definition changed, so the many switches performed after the manual stop never touched freeze-guard.service (its nix definition was unchanged) and left it stopped indefinitely. This timer is the fix: independent of whether a switch ever runs, periodically verify the PSI killer is active and restart it if not — closes the silent-disarm gap for good.

oomd._comment: systemd-oomd — PSI-aware proactive killer, THE evidence-based fix. The 2026-06-27 forensics (psi-recorder) showed the freezes were user.slice memory.pressure full-avg10 sustained at 62-68% for MINUTES with memory.events oom_kill=0 — the kernel throttled at MemoryHigh and swapped into 20G of swap forever while NOTHING ever killed. enable*Slice turns oomd on for -.slice/system.slice/user.slice, but its built-in default limit is 80% — ABOVE the 65% freeze, so it would never fire. pressure_limit OVERRIDES that to a value below the observed stall so oomd kills the worst cgroup BEFORE the machine locks. PSI is swap-independent, so 20G of swap cannot mask it. duration = sustained-seconds before the kill.

earlyoom._comment: earlyoom — DISABLED 2026-07-03 (user directive: 'remove ALL non-PSI triggers, ONLY PSI'). earlyoom has no PSI flag at all — it is purely absolute free-mem%/free-swap%, and repeatedly killed plasmashell on transient MemAvailable dips while /proc/pressure/memory sat near 0 (reclaim was keeping up fine, no real pressure — first tightened 5/3→2/1 as a partial fix, then fully disabled since ANY absolute threshold can still false-fire at PSI=0). The only two active killers now are systemd-oomd (memory PSI, pressure_limit=50%) and freeze-guard (mem/io/cpu PSI, 40/30/80 full-avg10/full-avg10/some-avg10) — both are genuinely PSI-gated per sysprot.watchdog's own contract ('PSI IS THE ONLY KILL METRIC'). enable=false is the single source of truth (services.earlyoom.enable reads this); flip to true + re-tune thresholds if a non-PSI last-resort backstop is ever wanted again.

sysctl._comment: Writeback + reclaim tuning. Lower dirty ratios flush dirty pages earlier and in smaller batches → no giant NVMe writeback burst that spikes iowait. vfs_cache_pressure<100 keeps dentry/inode cache longer → less metadata IO. min_free_kbytes/watermark keep a kernel reserve so allocation never stalls hard. swappiness 150 = prefer compressed zram over disk (zram is RAM-backed).

testers._comment: Run via the same data-driven runner pattern as test-session-checkpoint.sh. Each check proves one guarantee of the freeze-proof contract.

checks.description: nix-daemon cannot swap (build OOM-kills instead of thrashing the disk)
nix-daemon MemoryMax is the declared hard cap (not the 6G drift value)
user-1000.slice has guaranteed unreclaimable RAM (MemoryMin) so the desktop never freezes
user-1000.slice has a bounded 2G swap valve (zram-first) — not 0 (file-page thrash) and not unlimited (disk thrash)
user-1000.slice MemoryHigh is at least 4G — above the measured desktop working set (~3.5G), so no permanent memory.high reclaim throttle
the freeze-guard active PSI killer is running
freeze-guard is general-purpose — its deployed script reacts to CPU pressure, not just mem/io (grep the ExecStart store script; the unit text never contains it)
checks.command: grep -hE 'cpuPSI|psi_avg10' "$(systemctl show freeze-guard.service -p ExecStart --value | grep -oE '/nix/store/[^ ]*freeze-guard[^ ;]*' | head -1)" | head -1

checks.description: freeze-guard is in the untouchable island — can never be OOM-killed
freeze-guard runs in the reserved connectivity.slice island

the freeze-guard self-check timer is armed — re-arms the PSI killer within 60s if it's ever manually stopped and left off (2026-07-04 incident: a manual stop at 09:03 survived 3h22m and many nixos-rebuild switches because switch-to-configuration never restarts an unchanged-but-stopped unit)
earlyoom (non-PSI absolute-value killer) is disabled — only PSI-based killers (oomd, freeze-guard) may act
the untouchable island has guaranteed RAM for the killers + mesh
